Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated sizing — Helix workload summary

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the quick intro last week. As discussed, attaching a small export with a representative week of API traffic (sampled by request). High-level summary below — happy to clarify any of the fields.

- Avg requests/day: 120k
- Typical request size (prompt + expected generation): 800–2,400 tokens (median ~1,100)
- 95th pct context length we see: 6,000 tokens (longest tails for batch analysis)
- Concurrent active requests during peak windows: ~180 (10–15% of traffic concentrated in 30-minute windows)
- P95 latency target (end-to-end, generation only): <= 450 ms for the primary model in production
- Model mix today: single LLM model (13B int8), plan to add a 7B fast path for short completions

Questions for Redwood: given the above, what reserved commit size and GPU pool would you recommend for predictable latency and cost? Also curious about burst options for weekly analysis jobs and whether quantization to int8 would materially change the pool sizing.

Attachment: helix_request_samples.csv (CSV, 150KB)

Thanks,
Samir
Head of Platform — Helix Bio

Hi Samir — thanks for the export and the clear summary. Looping in Ben (solutions) and Marissa (pricing) so we can put together sizing + a committed quote. A few quick clarifying Qs before we size:

- Is the 6,000-token context mostly request-side (prompts), or do you include long function/tool output in that number?
- Are the weekly analysis jobs synchronous to your API (i.e., they share the same serving pool) or can they be scheduled on a separate burst pool?
- Do you have a preferred model mix day-to-day (percent of short vs long requests)? Even rough ratios help (e.g., 70% short <1k, 25% mid, 5% long).

I've normalized the sample and attached helix_workload_profile.csv — Ben/Marissa, please use that as the input for throughput modeling.

Next step: we'll produce two scenarios — a conservative guaranteed pool (for P95 latency SLO) and a hybrid plan with a smaller guaranteed pool + burst capacity (lower commit, higher burst). We can also show how an int8-only profile affects GPU count.

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 13:22:00 -0700
Subject: INTERNAL: Helix sizing + recommended pool (draft)

Marissa/Laura — I ran Helix's normalized profile through the throughput model. Notes and recommendation below (internal working draft; do not share externally until Laura signs off):

Workload assumptions (from helix_workload_profile.csv):
- Steady-state RPS during business hours: ~850 req/s
- Peak 30-minute window RPS: ~3,600 req/min (~60 req/s sustained during peak minute bursts; peaks concentrated within an hour)
- Median generation length: 1,100 tokens; p95 generation length: 4,500 tokens
- Expected concurrency per model instance: 6–8 active streams

Sizing summary (target: P95 <= 450 ms generation time for 13B int8 equivalent):
- Baseline guaranteed pool recommendation: 6x H100-80GB (or 8x A100-80GB equivalent)
  - Provides ~1.8M tokens/sec aggregate (model-dependent), supports ~150 concurrent in-flight sessions at 1k token avg while holding P95 latency target
- Hybrid option (lower commit + burst): 3x H100 guaranteed + 3x H100 burst (burst autoscale up to +100% for scheduled analysis)
  - This reduces committed cost ~45% but relies on burst availability for long tails
- If Helix switches primary model to smaller 7B fast-path for short completions (70% of traffic), baseline guaranteed pool drops to 3x H100 equivalent and tail load can be served by 2x A100 burst nodes

Pricing / commit guidance (preliminary):
- 12-month reserved commit (6x H100 baseline): estimated $115k/month list; we can consider a 15% commit discount for a signed 12-month deal (final pricing depends on exact GPU sku mix and utilization SLAs)
- 9-month pilot (3x H100 guaranteed + 3x burst): $62k/month list, discountable to ~12% given forecasted ARR and reference opportunity

Operational notes for the proposal:
- Recommend adding prefix KV caching for short requests — improves effective throughput by ~18% for Helix's short-path traffic
- Suggest a single canary rollout and a read-only reroute during the first 30 days to validate latency at scale

I'll convert this into an external-friendly email with explicit numbers (tokens/sec, expected concurrent slots) after Marissa weighs in on discounting.

Ben
Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

Thanks — helpful draft. Quick responses:
- The 6,000 tokens is almost entirely prompt/context (we pipeline a lot of historical notes into the prompt for long-run analyses). The model response is typically <800 tokens.
- Weekly analysis jobs are currently using the same cluster; we'd prefer them scheduled on a separate burst pool if possible.
- Model mix estimate for production: ~65% short (<1k tokens), 25% mid (1k–3k), 10% long (>3k)

A couple of asks from procurement:
1) If we do a 9-month pilot, can you confirm the discount floor and whether unused committed capacity rolls forward as credits?
2) For the int8/quantization scenario, how much lower can the committed GPU count realistically go (ballpark)?

Also — curious how SLAs change if we accept a hybrid (3x guarantee + burst) vs the 6x guaranteed pool.

Samir — really appreciate the clarifications. Action items and proposal below: 

1) Pilot proposal (recommended to start production validation quickly):
   - 9-month reserved commit: 3x H100 guaranteed + 3x H100 burst (burst capacity available during scheduled windows and handles weekly analysis jobs)
   - Pricing: list $62k/month; confirmed negotiable to a 12% committed discount for an executed 9-month agreement (final T&Cs in the MSA)
   - Credit policy: unused committed GPU-hours convert to billable credits usable within the 9-month term (no cash refunds). Rollover credits apply only within the active term.

2) 12-month committed alternative (if Helix wants lower unit price):
   - 6x H100 guaranteed; estimated $115k/month list; we can extend to 15% discount with reference and usage SLA commitments

3) Int8/quantization impact:
   - If Helix converts the primary production model to int8 (validated for quality), expected committed pool size reduces ~35–40% (e.g., 6x -> ~4x H100 equivalent). We will include a quantization test plan in the SOW to measure real gains.

4) SLA differences (summary):
   - Hybrid (3+3): standard availability SLA applies to the guaranteed pool; burst capacity is best-effort with scheduled availability windows and a service-level objective rather than an SLA-backed credit.
   - 6x guaranteed: higher uptime SLA on production traffic and guaranteed latency buckets for P95 (eligible for credits if missed).

Next steps: Laura to send official proposal with pool diagrams, explicit concurrency slots by model, and the pricing PDF. Can we schedule a 45-minute technical deep-dive on Mon 10 May to validate the quantization plan?

Attachment: redwood-dedicated-pricing-v2.pdf (PDF, 210KB)

Best,
